pins: account.graduated appears exactly once and LAST, after the fifth payout.win_days_reset and not the fourth, so R-49's `>=` is asserted at both boundaries by one stream; the ladder count itself is never written here and lives only in the plan record
note: THE LADDER COUNT IS NOT IN THIS FILE, WHICH IS GS-067's ROW GIVING AN INSTRUCTION RATHER THAN A DESCRIPTION. The row says the count "is the plan's, read from config, and stating it here would be a fourteenth copy of the value ADR-037 deleted the other thirteen of". So the expectation states five settlements and pins the event SEQUENCE; the number 5 appears in `payouts_settled_count` as a COUNT OF WHAT HAPPENED, never as the threshold. Lower `max_payouts` in `MERIT-RAPID-50K.json` and this fixture fails; a fixture that had copied the constant would have passed against a plan it no longer matched. THE EVENT LIST IS THE BOUNDARY PAIR AND THE END STATE IS NOT. `account.graduated` sits at position 21 of 21. An engine writing `>` instead of `>=` graduates at no settlement (5 > 5 is false), leaving the phase `funded` and the event absent. An engine graduating one rung early emits it at position 17, right after the fourth reset. BOTH FAIL HERE AND ONLY ONE OF THEM WOULD FAIL AN END-STATE-ONLY FIXTURE, because the early-graduation engine also ends in `graduated`. That asymmetry is why R-49's `>=` needs a sequence rather than a field. `trading_day` IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED, AND THE OMISSION IS A FINDING RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. R-49 graduates at DO-2 and M01 section 3.6 returns there because "no trading day follows", so the day's remaining steps never run. `applySettlement` builds its result by spreading the PRIOR state and never sets `tradingDay`, so the state carried out of the graduating day still names 2026-10-05 while `account.graduated` carries `tradingDay: 2026-10-06`. The state and its own event disagree about which day it is. M01 does not say which is right: R-49 states the phase change and the closure and says nothing about the row's date. A fixture pinning either value would ratify a reading nobody has made, so this one pins neither and records the disagreement. `traded_days_count: 15` AGAINST SIXTEEN MARKS IS THE SAME EARLY RETURN, MEASURED. The sixteenth day never reaches DO-6, so it advances no counter; it also carries `fill_count: 0`, so R-08 would not have counted it as traded even if the fold had continued. Both readings give 15 and the fixture does not depend on which one is doing the work. `withdrawable_cents: 0` IS R-35 ON A CLOSED ACCOUNT. The balance is 5,100,000 against a size of 5,000,000 and a buffer of 100,000, so an OPEN account would read exactly 0 here by arithmetic alone. That coincidence is the reason this field is weak evidence for the closure and is not offered as any: `phase: graduated` is the claim. `win_days_count: 0`, `consistency_best_day_cents: 0` AND `consistency_period_profit_cents: 0` ARE R-47 FIRING ON THE FIFTH SETTLEMENT WITH NOTHING AFTER IT. The reset runs at DO-2 and the day then returns, so no win day is earned back. This is the one shape in the directory where R-47's reset is observable in isolation, uncontaminated by the effective day's own trading, which is what GS-068 measures instead. `consistency_period_start_day: 2026-10-06` IS R-47 STARTING A PERIOD ON A CLOSED ACCOUNT, and it is stated rather than suppressed: the rule computes the next trading day after the basis day whether or not the ladder ended, and an engine that special-cased graduation would write null. `payout_anchor_day: 2026-10-05` AND `cadence_anchor_day: 2026-10-06` ARE R-46's TWO DATES DIFFERING AGAIN, here across an ordinary overnight rather than a holiday. `lifetime_settled_cents: 500000` IS R-50 SUMMED OVER FIVE CAPPED EXTRACTIONS, and it equals INV-17's bound of `ladder * max cap` exactly. THAT IS NOT THIS FIXTURE'S CLAIM: GS-241 owns the assertion that no sequence can EXCEED the bound. This file asserts only what R-50 accumulated along the path it walked, and the two claims are about the same number for different reasons. `floor_cents: 4950000`, `high_water_balance_cents: 5200000` AND `floor_locked: false` ARE R-48 HOLDING ACROSS FIVE SETTLEMENTS RATHER THAN ONE. GS-081 measured the three untouched fields across a single payout on a locked account; this is the trailing-floor case repeated five times, where a floor that moved by any amount per settlement would have drifted 5 times as far and be unmissable. The high-water balance is 5,200,000 because the account reached it on 2026-09-17 and never closed higher: each cycle climbs back to exactly the level the previous payout left it below.
